process_policy.rule: R4 follow-up F1(b) (reviews/REVIEW_PREFREEZE_R4_FOLLOWUP_P309.md): process execution is ALLOWLISTED. A call that can start a process or run git is a finding unless it lies in an exactly-once site or in a function listed in reviewed_functions (file, qualified name, AST sha256, permits, reason), or it is a git call whose verb is a literal in git_read_verbs (with literal options only; the conditional read forms of symbolic-ref, config, branch, remote, worktree, sparse-checkout and stash are recognised by their arguments). Unknown verbs are ref-moving (REF_MUTATION_UNLISTED unless listed in ref_mutation_functions); git_object_verbs need the git_write permit (or a ref_mutation_functions listing). os.system/popen/exec*/spawn*/posix_spawn*/fork*, pty.spawn, asyncio.create_subprocess_*, subprocess attributes other than run/Popen/call/check_call/check_output, and shell=True are always findings. Aliases of process functions or modules, getattr/vars on them, __import__/import_module of them or with non-literal names, exec/eval/compile of non-literal code, git runners used as values, forbidden git options, and filesystem writes whose target is built from a git directory are findings. A `python -c` code string and a literal exec/eval/compile string are parsed and scanned with every rule. Every file of the scanned tree has an allowed suffix and no executable bit, and no module shadows a research module. Entries are added only by review; code/p309_scan_pins.py refreshes the AST hashes of listed entries before the freeze only.
